title: South Africa
capsule: The Union of South Africa was established on 31 May 1910, merging the former British colonies of the Cape and Natal with the Boer republics of the Transvaal and Orange River Colony; it became a republic outside the Commonwealth in 1961. The country's 20th-century history was dominated by apartheid, a statutory racial classification system formalized by the National Party after its 1948 electoral victory under D. F. Malan and progressively tightened through the 1960s under Hendrik Verwoerd. International sanctions, sustained internal resistance led by the ANC and allied organizations, and the release of Nelson Mandela in February 1990 precipitated negotiations that produced the first non-racial elections of April 1994, after which Mandela was inaugurated as the country's first democratically elected president. The dataset attests South Africa's geometry from 1932 through the present, reflecting post-1931 Statute of Westminster full sovereignty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Post-1910 boundaries are based on formal colonial and then republican cartographic records and are precisely known; the 1932 start date in this dataset corresponds to the period after the Statute of Westminster and is administratively well-documented.
